newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Mir commander says situation stabilised at last.
newsitem.headline: Mir commander says situation stabilised at last.

text.p: The commander of the Mir space station said on Friday the situation on the Russian craft had finally stabilised after an accident on Wednesday that damaged its electric power supply and holed one of it modules.

"For the first time, I feel that the situation on the station has stabilised," a spokeswoman at Mission Control near Moscow quoted Vasily Tsibliyev as telling the centre after checking the air pressure, temperature and humidity.

The spokeswoman, who said earlier on Friday that the crew had taken turns in sleeping, said Tsibliyev woke up at 5 a.m. Moscow time (0100 GMT), two hours before his colleagues, and started checking the main instruments.

A committee including NASA officials and Mir's designer met early on Friday to try to work out a concrete plan of action to mend the damage and to detail preparations for the launch of a cargo ship which is due to deliver repair supplies to Mir.
A committee member said the main task was to place orders with different Russian firms to produce the necessary equipment. "The work is very complicated," he said, declining to be named.

No date is yet set for the launch from Russia's Baikonur cosmodrome in Kazakhstan. The official said the ship, which was previously due to start a routine mission on Friday, could sit on the launch pad for 10 days but would need several days for refuelling and checks if it was held up beyond than that.
